name: John Taylor
role: Apostle wounded at Carthage, later Church president
dateNote: He was called to the Twelve in July 1838 and ordained that December; he was wounded at Carthage on 27 June 1844.
importance: Section 118 names him to fill a vacancy in the Twelve in July 1838. Section 124 lists him with the Twelve at Nauvoo. He was in the Carthage Jail room when Joseph and Hyrum Smith were killed, and section 135 reports he was badly wounded. Section 138 names him among the leaders seen in Joseph F. Smith’s vision.
connections: Parley P. Pratt baptized him in Canada in 1836. Willard Richards was with him at Carthage, and he later succeeded Brigham Young as Church president.

sources.title: John Taylor, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 1 Nov. 1808, Milnthorpe, England; baptized 9 May 1836; ordained apostle 19 Dec. 1838 at Far West; at Carthage 27 June 1844; Church president from 1877 (ordained 1880); died July 1887 at Kaysville, Utah. Wounds are from D&C 135:2. Section 135 is traditionally attributed to him, but the official heading names no author.
